newsitem.title: GERMANY: Two Germans held after Syrian stabbed to death.
newsitem.headline: Two Germans held after Syrian stabbed to death.

text.p: Two German men stabbed to death a Syrian asylum-seeker in a vegetable shop after he tried to protect two female assistants, prosecutors said.
The men, aged 18 and 20, were remanded in custody on Friday on accusations they taunted the women in the shop in the eastern city of Leipzig late on Wednesday evening, calling them "Turkish bitches".
When the 30-year-old Syrian, who also worked in the store, went to help them they stabbed him in the chest with a 30 cm-long (12 inch) kitchen knife, a prosecutors' spokesman said.
They were arrested near the shop after fleeing. On Friday flower tributes lay outside the shop's closed doors.
Prosecutors declined to specify a motive for the killing.
After German unification in 1990 there was a three-year upsurge of neo-Nazi violence. More than 30 people died, including the victims of firebomb attacks on Turkish homes in Solingen and Moelln.
